_what: Trillion's screens drawn inside an AI app (ChatGPT, Claude) through the MCP Apps standard (src/screen-view.mjs, src/workspace/screen-view.tsx). `view` is the one view document every screen is drawn in: its ui:// address, the fixed script and stylesheet addresses it loads from this service (fixed because an AI app keeps the document between deploys), and its height inside a chat: every tool result opens the full workspace in `whole_px`, including the controls inside the host height allowance. Full screen asks the host for a larger box without changing the workspace. `compact_px` and `expanded_px` remain for older view scripts. `reads` are the addresses a screen drawn there may read and change through the app's own sign-in (the screen_read tool): the workspace's own reads, minus what is done only in Trillion itself (sign-in methods, keys, saved logins, devices). `tools` names the tools whose answer is shown as a screen: each row's `address` is a workspace address made of its parts, a text or a value read `from` the tool's input or result by `field`; a tool whose answer lacks a needed value shows the row's `otherwise` address when it has one, else no screen. A row with `result_screen: true` instead declares that its owner returns the exact destination under `trillion/screen`; the shared adapter validates that destination and advertises the renderer before the call, without a separate show_screen call. An omitted target selects no screen (for example, deliberate save-only); static host metadata may still open an outer panel. `whole` names the workspace itself without requiring a selected screen. Every ordinary screen result also opens in that same shared workspace (the person's sidebar and arrangement, src/workspace/mount-workspace.ts), with the exact requested screen and input selected. `words` are what the person and the app read. Every successfully opened screen also carries a quiet Open in Trillion control for the same address; the view counts shown, pressed and full-open moments through the shared interaction store. `placements` are the places an AI app can open a screen from besides the model's own call, as data: each place names the entrypoint type the host calls it (ChatGPT: home is its sidebar entry, `global`; side-panel is a tab beside a conversation, `thread`), and a `tools` row lists the places its screen sits in, with the title the host shows (a side panel's title is never the app's own name). src/screen-view.mjs turns these rows into each host's entrypoints; a host opens such a tool with no input, so a row with a placement must run with none.
